newsitem.title: INDIA: India call money rates seen moving up soon - I-Sec.
newsitem.headline: India call money rates seen moving up soon - I-Sec.

text.p: Indian call money rates are likely to firm up soon as surplus liquidity gets drained from the banking system, ICICI Securities and Finance Co (I-Sec) said in a report on Monday.
"Call money rates have been below 1.0 percent levels for most of the previous fortnight," I-Sec said.

The surplus funds in the system could be attributed to strong growth in bank deposits, central bank intervention in the foreign exchange market and the discontinuation of treasury bills available on tap with the Reserve Bank of India, it said.

"We should see more realistic call money rates as the surplus liquidity gets gradually absorbed through government borrowings, open market operations and the new treasury bills proposed in the monetary policy," I-Sec said.
The Reserve Bank of India, in its monetary and credit policy for first half 1997/98 (April-March) issued last Tuesday, announced it would introduce treasury bills of different maturities.
